correctness.rationale: For every k>=2,N>=k+1,gamma>0 the q1,q2 Hessian block has determinant one, hence H_gamma is SPD, and the exact V-reduced Hessian is I_2. Gaussian LS regression z=(X^T X)^-1 X^T y has isotropic two-dimensional density (k-1)/(2pi)(1+||z||^2)^(-(k+1)/2), giving radial survival (1+t^2)^(-(k-1)/2). Symmetrization yields Hhat=I_2+gamma[[z1,z2/2],[z2/2,0]] with lower eigenvalue 1+gamma(z1-||z||)/2; J_2 Hhat has a positive real eigenvalue iff Hhat is indefinite. Uniform Gaussian direction gives arcsine c=(1-cos(theta))/2 and the stated exact one-dimensional probability. Dominated convergence at gamma down to 0 and boundary Laplace asymptotics at c=1 yield sharp constants for k large. Independent numerical integration matched 60,000-sample Gaussian regression experiments for k=2,3,5 within sampling error; Monte Carlo alone cannot prove the all-k integral.
residual_risks: Finite checks are corroborations only; analytic proof establishes universal parameters.
